Q: HTML to PDF print using Chromium A:

Chrome only knows its own domain and any other domain it is told to use.

Thus by default with the smallest example will write in its own folder a file called output.pdf.
chrome --headless --print-to-pdf www.example.com

Thus, the first task is EITHER ensuring the file can be written in its own domain or tell it to use a user folder and name.

This means for Windows users --print-to-pdf="%cd%/example.pdf" or for bash --print-to-pdf="${PWD}/example.pdf" will go to users' domain

That sorts the where to write problems. The next problem is what is allowed for the source URL? I showed it does not have to be https:// it will often assume www.example.com is remote. However, we may get unexpected results!

We can see that if the frame points to iframe.src = "https://www.example.com"; and command is

chrome --headless --print-to-pdf="%cd%/example.pdf"  file://%cd%/wrapper.html

That is not allowed as crossing domains.

Thus we need to say for local input file://folder/file.svg or .html or .xml etc. but normally it cannot be a "wrapper" of another.

Thus the print-to-pdf source must be the top level

chrome --headless --print-to-pdf="${PWD}/example.pdf"  "file://${PWD}/my.html"

You can then add any other refinements including timers and remove print header add outline etc. (--run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw --virtual-time-budget=80000 --no-pdf-header-footer --generate-pdf-document-outline)

Thus print to pdf this page.

This use of Chrome is heavy and slow it is better to do the same using Chrome-Headless-Shell (naturally without --headless command). It is many times faster.

Q: Folder Migration from one Windows PC to another using python script A:

SOURCE_ROOT = Path("D:\\") points to the local D: drive on the destination PC, not the source machine.

To copy from another PC you must use a UNC path (or a mapped network drive), e.g.:

SOURCE_ROOT = Path(r"\\OLD-PC\D$")

Right now Python is checking D:\dgarrard on the destination PC, which doesn’t exist, hence “Source not found”.

Verify access first:

dir \\OLD-PC\D$\dgarrard

If that works, the script will too.
